summary: msgpack-ruby JRuby decoder makes uncapped header-count allocations; a 5-byte message forces multi-GiB OOM
details:
### Summary

The **JRuby** implementation of msgpack (`msgpack` gem, `java` platform — pure Java decoder under `ext/java/`) sizes containers directly from the element count written in the message header, with **no cap at all**: no equivalent of the C unpacker's `SHRT_MAX` clamp (since 1.7.3) and none of the buffered-bytes cap that commit c8d42d8 added for CRuby in 1.8.6. A single 5-byte message decides how much memory a JVM process tries to allocate:

* `array32` header declaring `0x7FFFFFFF` elements → `new IRubyObject[0x7FFFFFFF]` (~8 GiB of reference slots) attempted immediately → `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Requested array size exceeds VM limit`.
* Counts *below* the VM's max-array-size but above available heap (e.g. 5×10⁸ with a 512 MiB heap) produce a **real allocation attempt** — `OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` — the JVM genuinely tries to take the memory before failing.
* `str32`/`bin32` headers declaring `0x7FFFFFFF` bytes do the same via `readBytes(size)` → `new byte[size]`.
* Below the failure threshold there is a **silent band**: one streaming unpacker fed only an `array32` header with count 2×10⁷ (5 wire bytes, zero elements) grows used heap **+78 MiB immediately**, no exception (`each` swallows the underflow), and the footprint stays elevated after `Unpacker#reset` + full GC. Linear in declared count (~4 B/element); nothing bounds it — not delivered bytes, not a per-container cap.

Only counts ≥ 2³¹ are refused (a clean `MessagePack::UnderflowError` from `getUnsignedInt()`), and only **maps** are safe (`consumeHash` grows per element instead of pre-sizing). Verified on the released gem `msgpack 1.8.6 java`, JRuby 9.4.12 / OpenJDK 25, 2026-10-30 — i.e. **unfixed in the current release**. Proposed fix mirrors c8d42d8: cap initial allocation by bytes actually buffered and grow as data arrives; read strings in bounded chunks instead of allocating the declared length up front.


### Details

### 1. The four dispatch arms, and which pre-allocate (line numbers at tag v1.8.6 — current release; `ext/java` has no commits after it)

| header | dispatch ([Decoder.java](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-ruby/blob/v1.8.6/ext/java/org/msgpack/jruby/Decoder.java)) | behaviour on the declared count | measured (released 1.8.6-java, Xmx512m) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `array32` `\xdd` | [:296](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-ruby/blob/v1.8.6/ext/java/org/msgpack/jruby/Decoder.java#L296) → [`consumeArray(int size)` :139-145](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-ruby/blob/v1.8.6/ext/java/org/msgpack/jruby/Decoder.java#L139-L145) | `new IRubyObject[size]` **immediately**, before reading any element | count `0x7FFFFFFF`: OOME "Requested array size exceeds VM limit"; count 5×10⁸: OOME "**Java heap space**" (real allocation attempt); count 2×10⁷: **+78 MiB, silent** |
| `str32` `\xdb` | [:294](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-ruby/blob/v1.8.6/ext/java/org/msgpack/jruby/Decoder.java#L294) → [`consumeString` :129](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-ruby/blob/v1.8.6/ext/java/org/msgpack/jruby/Decoder.java#L129) → [`readBytes(int size)` :186-190](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-ruby/blob/v1.8.6/ext/java/org/msgpack/jruby/Decoder.java#L186-L190) | `new byte[size]` **immediately** | len `0x7FFFFFFF`: OOME "array size exceeds VM limit" |
| `bin32` `\xc6` | [:269](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-ruby/blob/v1.8.6/ext/java/org/msgpack/jruby/Decoder.java#L269) → same `consumeString`/`readBytes` | same | len `0x7FFFFFFF`: OOME "array size exceeds VM limit" |
| `map32` `\xdf` | [:298](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-ruby/blob/v1.8.6/ext/java/org/msgpack/jruby/Decoder.java#L298) → [`consumeHash(int size)` :147+](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-ruby/blob/v1.8.6/ext/java/org/msgpack/jruby/Decoder.java#L147) | **no pre-allocation** — inserts per element, underflows on first missing byte | count `0x7FFFFFFF`: no exception (swallowed), no large allocation |

The only guard is [`getUnsignedInt()` :88-94](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-ruby/blob/v1.8.6/ext/java/org/msgpack/jruby/Decoder.java#L88-L94): counts with the top bit set (≥ 2³¹) raise `MessagePack::UnderflowError: Size too large (limited to 2**31 for the Java version)`. That bounds the *value* but leaves the entire positive band `(available heap, 2³¹)` unbounded — and that band is where real allocation attempts happen.

### 2. Contrast with the C implementation (same repo)

The CRuby unpacker has had a per-container cap since 1.7.3 (`INITIAL_BUFFER_CAPACITY_MAX = SHRT_MAX`) and, since [c8d42d8](https://github.com/msgpack/msgpack-ruby/commit/c8d42d8) in **1.8.6**, additionally caps initial size by bytes actually buffered ("an element needs at least one byte…"). Strings on C are bounded too (`read_raw_body_cont` allocates `min(remaining, buffered)`). The Java decoder has **neither generation of cap** — it is strictly behind the CRuby behaviour this repo already considers correct enough to ship.

### 3. Silent retention + mechanism control (measured 2026-10-30, released gem)

One `MessagePack::Unpacker` per process, fed only a header (`"\xdd" + [count].pack('N')`), zero elements; heap = `Runtime.total_memory - free_memory` after `GC.start` on both sides:

| declared count | used heap before → after | delta | exception? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000,000 | 26.4 → 31.1 MiB | +4.7 | none (`each` swallows the underflow) |
| 5,000,000 | 53.3 → 74.0 MiB | +20.7 | none |
| 20,000,000 | 51.3 → 129.3 MiB | **+78.0** | none |

Mechanism control: after the feed, `Unpacker#reset` + three `GC.start` cycles left used heap at **+79.4 MiB above baseline** (2×10⁷ arm) — the elevation is *not* unpacker-held state; it is JVM heap already spent on header-declared allocation and not returned. Either way the process footprint grows per attack and stays grown; the peak cost is paid synchronously during parsing regardless of GC behaviour afterwards. (Honest scope note: this is unbounded **allocation**, not a memory leak.)

### 4. Why JVM makes availability impact worse than the CRuby analogue

In CRuby, allocation failure raises `NoMemoryError`/fails inside one worker process. In a JVM, an OOME raised on the parser thread can land anywhere in the host application's shared runtime — long-lived JRuby servers (Rails, Logstash-class pipelines, JDBC apps) share heap across all threads and connections; a single crafted message can destabilize or kill the whole JVM, not just the request. The silent band means no exception at all is even required to spend memory.

### 5. Not claimed / scope

* **Fluentd is NOT affected** (and this report deliberately does not involve it): Fluentd ships CRuby-only — CI pins `engine: cruby`, gemspec requires ruby >= 3.3 while JRuby 9.4 implements Ruby 3.1 semantics, and there are zero JRUBY guards in lib/. This is an upstream msgpack-ruby report only.
* Maps (`map32`) do not pre-allocate — measured; the class applies to `array32`/`str32`/`bin32`.
* Counts ≥ 2³¹ are cleanly refused — measured; no claim there.
* Older java-gem releases were not individually probed; `<= 1.8.6` means "every release up to the current one carries this code".


### Proof of concept

Verified on the **released gem** `msgpack 1.8.6 java`, JRuby 9.4.12.0, OpenJDK 25.0.4.1, Linux x86-64 (artifacts in `evidence_186_recheck/`). Always run with a small `-Xmx` so oversized requests fail fast instead of wrecking the box.

### Setup

```console
$ curl -fsSLO https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/jruby/jruby-dist/9.4.12.0/jruby-dist-9.4.12.0-bin.tar.gz
$ tar xzf jruby-dist-9.4.12.0-bin.tar.gz && export PATH=$PWD/jruby-9.4.12.0/bin:$PATH
$ jruby -S gem install msgpack --no-document      # resolves the java-platform gem: "msgpack (1.8.6 java)"
```

### 1. Header shapes (fresh process per arm, `-Xmx512m`)

```console
array32 count=0xFFFFFFFF       -> MessagePack::UnderflowError: Size too large (limited to 2**31 for the Java version)
array32 count=0x7FFFFFFF       -> Java::JavaLang::OutOfMemoryError: Requested array size exceeds VM limit
array32 count=500000000        -> Java::JavaLang::OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space   # real allocation attempt
str32   len=0x7FFFFFFF         -> Java::JavaLang::OutOfMemoryError: Requested array size exceeds VM limit
bin32   len=0x7FFFFFFF         -> Java::JavaLang::OutOfMemoryError: Requested array size exceeds VM limit
map32   count=0x7FFFFFFF       -> no exception, no large allocation (consumeHash grows per element)
```

Each payload is five bytes, e.g. `"\xdd" + [count].pack('N')` fed to `MessagePack::Unpacker#feed_each`. Scripts: `jr_probe.rb`, `jr_probe_extra.rb` (attached in kit).

### 2. Silent band — retention from one header (Xmx1g)

```console
$ for n in 1000000 5000000 20000000; do jruby -J-Xmx1g jr_one.rb $n; done
count=  1000000 heap 26.4 -> 31.1 MiB (delta 4.7)   | no exception (underflow swallowed)
count=  5000000 heap 53.3 -> 74.0 MiB (delta 20.7)  | no exception (underflow swallowed)
count= 20000000 heap 51.3 -> 129.3 MiB (delta 78.0) | no exception (underflow swallowed)

$ jruby -J-Xmx1g jr_reset_control.rb 20000000
count=20000000 heap base=49.9 after_feed=129.3 (delta 79.4) after_reset_gc=129.3 (retained_vs_base 79.4)
```

A streaming server that keeps one unpacker per connection (the pattern any socket-fed msgpack service uses) pays this per connection with five wire bytes each and produces no exception, no log line.

### 3. Fix verification path

Apply the C-side idea from c8d42d8: in `consumeArray`, cap the initial array by bytes actually buffered (an element needs ≥ 1 byte) and grow as elements arrive; in `readBytes`/`consumeString`, read in bounded chunks instead of allocating the declared length up front. Then re-run this PoC: the silent band should track delivered bytes, and oversized declarations should raise `UnderflowError`-class errors without touching multi-GiB allocations. msgpack-ruby CI runs jruby-9.4/truffleruby, so a patch is verifiable as-is; I can prepare one against `ext/java/org/msgpack/jruby/Decoder.java`.


### Impact

**Type.** Uncontrolled resource consumption driven by *declared* sizes rather than delivered bytes — CWE-770 (Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling), precisely CWE-1325 (Independent Resource Usage Limiting Not Applied). Availability only; no confidentiality/integrity impact, no code execution.

**Who is impacted.** Any JRuby application that feeds untrusted msgpack to `MessagePack.unpack`/`Unpacker` — the java-platform gem's whole user base (JRuby-based services, log/RPC pipelines, JVM polyglot stacks using this gem). For them: remote OOM of a shared-heap JVM from a 5-byte message, or silent heap spend below the exception band.

**Severity.** Proposed **High / 7.5**, `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` — remote, trivially crafted, default settings, process death; same metric string as the accepted fluentd OOM family (e.g. GHSA-h3xv-5jpx-r4j2) and as this repo's own C-side analogue (reported separately, patched at 1.8.6). If triage weighs the platform scope (java gem only), lower framings read against that — we flag it honestly; the maintainers' call on scope shouldn't delay the patch.

**Relationship to the C-side report.** Same flaw class, different implementation and fix state: CRuby's pre-allocation was capped by c8d42d8 (released 1.8.6, separate advisory with affected `<= 1.8.5`, patched `1.8.6`). This JRuby variant is **unfixed in 1.8.6** and needs its own patch + CVE. Cross-reference both ways once filed.

**What this is not.** Not a Fluentd issue (Fluentd is CRuby-only — CI pins cruby, gemspec ruby >= 3.3 vs JRuby's Ruby 3.1 semantics); no fluentd advisory should carry this. Not a memory leak (measured: footprint elevation persists after reset+GC without retained objects). Not exploitable via maps or counts ≥ 2³¹ (both measured safe/cleanly refused).
